# CRITICAL RULES — DELIVERY ROUTING

1. CLAUDE, BEFORE GENERATING OR REQUESTING: Search this catalog by game need (heroes, terrain, UI, etc.) and open the actual existing image(s). If art quality is present in a flattened concept, request a clean extraction/production adaptation, not brand-new primitive approximations. Do NOT use the rejected C02 sprites as a visual model.

2. ASSET PRODUCER, ON DELIVERY: Pick an ID/version, write files into a functional art folder, and add a direct catalog entry HERE with title, status, exact link, source request, intended use, dimension/format, limitations and superseded versions. Update the index before marking the request DELIVERED.

3. CLAUDE, WHEN IMPLEMENTING: Check this catalog again and read the completed request. An existing usable source should be preferred to a poor later version. After integration, note actual GitHub path/commit if known. Do not claim a Drive upload is automatically live in Railway.

4. EVERY MATERIAL CHANGE: Dated Eastern-time changelog entry with links to the updated catalog + asset folder/request. Add a change even when a previously indexed asset is rejected or superseded, and update current recommended entry rather than leave stale default.

5. DEFAULT APPROVAL: New art may be used and revised without asking the owner. That DOES NOT bypass visual quality: producers must examine pixels and compare to approved visual references; a flat image is not an importable atlas. If poor, keep quality request open and revise. Old rejected assets stay rejected.

# STATUS DEFINITIONS

STRONG REFERENCE: Visual benchmark/flattened scene/artboard; use to design, extract and rebuild, not claim engine import ready.

IMPORTABLE PROTOTYPE: Real separated PNGs/JSON/audio with proven file structure; revise visual quality as needed.

QUALITY VERIFIED / GAME READY: Only after seeing the actual deliverable at iPhone gameplay scale and validating frames/layers/transparency/consistency. None of old rejected C02 art qualifies.

REJECTED: Never present as a positive visual source; grid/technical format may be read if needed.

EXPLORATORY: Useful potential context, not a locked game or final design decision.
